subject: Renewal proposal: phased capacity increase + credit rebalance for Cortex Labs
messages:
From: Ava Li <ava.li@cortexlabs.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal discussion: Q4 capacity & overage buffer

Hi Diego,

Hope you had a good weekend. We're running into sustained higher inference volume and expect a mid-Q4 uplift across a couple of product lines. Two items we'd like to discuss for our September renewal: 1) a short-term capacity top-up effective immediately (approx +55% to our current committed units) and 2) how to co-term that top-up into our annual renewal without a large billing shock.

Can you share the options you typically offer for a mid-contract uplift and if there are short-term credit or smoothing options to avoid a major one-time invoice? Attached: Cortex_usage_Q2-Q3.pdf (usage summary).

Cheers,
Ava Li
Head of Platform Engineering
Cortex Labs

Attachment: Cortex_usage_Q2-Q3.pdf (report, 2.1 MB)

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Ava Li <ava.li@cortexlabs.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion: Q4 capacity & overage buffer

Hi Ava — thanks for the data and context, that's helpful. High level, we can approach this three ways (quick summary here; I'll pull together a draft term sheet and run numbers with finance):

1) Immediate prorated top-up: add the +55% capacity now, prorated to your next renewal date, standard uplift discount of 10% on the incremental units for the remainder of the term. One-time invoice for the prorated months.

2) Staged top-up + smoothing credits: implement a smaller immediate top-up (+30%) and schedule the remainder to kick at renewal, with Redwood issuing a usage credit spread across the remaining months to reduce invoice spike. Typically ~15% credit on incremental units if you commit to the co-term at renewal.

3) Annualize now (co-term early): convert the uplift into an annualized commit and co-term to your renewal date for a deeper discount (we can go up to 18–22% on blended pricing depending on term length and commit). This reduces administrative churn but requires a longer commitment.

I'll attach a first-pass term sheet (draft_term_sheet_v1.pdf) and flag the three options with ballpark $ numbers after I sync with Marissa/Ben. If you have a preference for smoothing vs committing, call it out and we'll tailor.

Happy to jump on a quick call this week if that's easier.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachment: draft_term_sheet_v1.pdf (stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-01T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion: Q4 capacity & overage buffer — recommended path

Diego / Ben — quick internal recommendation based on Cortex's usage profile and renewal cadence:

- Recommended primary: Option 2 (Staged top-up + smoothing credits). Rationale: Cortex signals short-term demand but is sensitive to cashflow and procurement cycles. Offer a +30% immediate add, then roll remaining +25% into the renewal as a co-term annualized commit.

- Pricing mechanics: 12% discount on immediate incremental units, and an additional 12% smoothing credit applied over the prorated months (effectively ~18% across the uplift when amortized). At renewal, convert the remaining uplift into a 12-month commit at a blended discount of 15% (higher if they sign a 24-month).

- One-time concession: offer a $15k onboarding/ingestion credit (to cover migration runbook + extra SRE support). This is non-recurring and should be applied only if Cortex signs the co-term by Oct 10.

- Approvals needed: Ben (pricing) sign-off for the 12% smoothing credit; Monica (finance) to confirm invoice cadence + how credit amortization looks in billing. Legal to own contract amendment timeline (~7–10 business days).

Numbers: for transparency, if we take their reported Jul-Aug run-rate and add the +55% uplift fully today, the one-time invoice (prorated 3 months left in term) lands ~ $136k before credits; with the staged approach and credits it becomes ~$92k effective spread over the next 3 months (net of credits).

If you want I can craft the specific line items to drop into the term sheet.

-Marissa
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

(On internal approvals)
